# Semantic Fact Layer

- Private bitwise zero-minus shift supported-nonnegative count bitwise-not OR counterpart deep-chain inference is now modularized without changing the accepted semantic fact surface or local LSP query behavior. The behavior-preserving split moves the zero-minus / unary-minus zero-minus bitwise-not OR counterpart deep helper chain into internal `type_inference_bitwise_identity_bitwise_not_or_counterpart_deep.c/.h`, while `type_inference_bitwise_identity_bitwise_not_or_counterpart.c` keeps safe negation, unary-minus direct leaf, zero-wrapper skipper, and the public dispatcher. No parser or LSP cases were added or removed: the private parser target remains 260 cases and the private-mask LSP target remains 224 queries. WSL gcc and WSL clang isolated focused validation passed private parser 260 tests / 0 failures plus private-mask LSP PASS; Windows MSVC validation passed the same focused pair under `build-msvc-lsp-bitwise-zero` with `VSCMD_VER=17.14.34`. Public headers, ordinary supported-count files, private mask count-side readers, wrapped supported-count readers, global zero-wrapper stripping, semantic facts, arbitrary normalization, fixed point, and CFG-wide loop dataflow remain unchanged. Full repository GREEN is not claimed.

`SZrSemanticContext` 是编译期语义事实的唯一共享容器。parser、type inference、semantic analyzer 负责把表达式类型、引用、数值、可达性、逻辑和所有权事实写入这里；LSP 已开始查询这些事实，Debug 和 REPL 已开始接入同一诊断/表达式方向，完整事实复用仍在后续推进，避免各自复制一套局部推断规则。

- Private bitwise zero-minus shift supported-nonnegative count zero-minus and unary-minus zero-minus bitwise-not one-sided all-ones OR zero-minus unary-minus zero-minus unary-minus zero-minus unary-minus zero-minus unary-minus zero-minus unary-minus zero-minus unary-minus zero-minus unary-minus zero-minus zero-minus bitwise-not direct leaf operand publication now lets the private bitwise-not exact-all-ones OR leaf reader accept an OR counterpart proven as exact-zero-left `zero -` over the existing 06:09 unary-minus deep counterpart leaf. The existing private parser target `zr_vm_bitwise_zero_minus_shift_supported_count_private_bitwise_not_mask_operand_range_inference_test` / `zr_vm_bzms_private_not_mask_range_test` expands from 252 to 260 cases, and the private-mask LSP target `zr_vm_lsp_bzms_private_not_mask_query_test` expands from 216 to 224 query cases. The new parser coverage continues in `bitwise_zero_minus_shift_supported_count_private_not_mask_or_deep_leaf_cases.c/.h` instead of growing the 1016-line OR-leaf cases file; the new LSP coverage extends the existing deep query helper to 80 deep queries, and the deep parser helper now registers 72 tests. New coverage accepts `zero - (-(zero - (-(zero - (-(zero - (-(zero - (-(zero - (-(zero - (-(zero - (zero - (~negativeFour))))))))))))))))` as the non-all-ones side of one-sided all-ones OR leaves inside zero-minus and unary-minus zero-minus bitwise-not exact-all-ones operand chains, publishing `2..3` for outer zero-minus RHS and `-3..-2` for zero-minus unary-RHS. The implementation stays in the split internal counterpart module: the new private `type_inference_bitwise_identity_expression_zero_minus_unary_minus_zero_minus_unary_minus_zero_minus_unary_minus_zero_minus_unary_minus_zero_minus_unary_minus_zero_minus_unary_minus_zero_minus_unary_minus_zero_minus_zero_minus_bitwise_not_direct_leaf_int64_range` requires an exact-zero left side, delegates the right side to the 06:09 unary-minus counterpart reader, reuses the safe negation guard, and runs after that reader and before the same-identifier fallback. The counterpart module is now 925 lines; this slice keeps it cohesive because the new branch belongs to the same private deep counterpart chain, but the next addition to that chain should first extract a deep alternating counterpart module. Public headers, ordinary supported-count target files, the private mask count-side reader, wrapped supported-count readers, global zero-wrapper skipper, non-exact bitwise-not operands, different-identifier structural equality, arbitrary non-all-ones operands, nonzero-left zero-minus, arbitrary subtraction, arbitrary negative operands, negative or out-of-range shift counts, nonzero-left shifts, unsupported count algebra, arbitrary expression normalization, fixed-point convergence, and CFG-wide loop dataflow remain unchanged. TDD evidence: WSL gcc focused build passed first, then the expanded private parser target stabilized at 8 new semantic failures out of 260 tests and the expanded private-mask LSP target reported the eight old `0..0` range facts. After the new counterpart reader, WSL gcc passed private parser 260 tests / 0 failures plus private-mask LSP PASS; WSL clang passed the same focused pair; Windows MSVC validation passed focused build/run under `build-msvc-lsp-bitwise-zero` with `buildParser=0 buildLsp=0 parser=0 lsp=0` and `VSCMD_VER=17.14.34`. Full repository GREEN is not claimed.

## Stage 2 Diagnostic Fix Foundation

2026-07-18 update: the first ordered diagnostic-structure item from `02-diagnostics-and-errors.md` section 1 is now implemented across parser, semantic analyzer, LSP materialization, and stdio JSON. `SZrStructuredDiagnostic`, `SZrDiagnostic`, and `SZrLspDiagnostic` carry `fixes` plus `descriptorId`; each fix carries a title, source/edit range, replacement text, and one of `UNKNOWN`, `MACHINE_APPLICABLE`, `HAS_PLACEHOLDERS`, or `MAYBE_INCORRECT`. Construction, copying, range conversion, and freeing are explicit at each ownership boundary. Parser fix construction, semantic-analyzer copying, and LSP copying live in focused modules so the already-large orchestration files do not gain another responsibility; `diagnostic_builder.c` is 997 physical lines after extraction.

Definite-assignment read diagnostics are the first consumer. Both `uninitialized_read` and `possibly_uninitialized_read` retain their declaration `relatedInformation` and now add `Replace with an initialized value`, replacing the read range with `<value>`. The applicability is `HAS_PLACEHOLDERS`, so the edit is an IDE-visible template and must not be silently batch-applied. LSP conversion translates the parser byte range through the document position codec. Stdio publication keeps standard `Diagnostic` fields unchanged and stores `descriptorId` plus fix title, standard-shaped `TextEdit` (`range`/`newText`), and applicability in opaque `Diagnostic.data`. The descriptor value remains `0` until the planned diagnostic registry is implemented; this slice establishes transport and lifecycle, not registry assignment.

TDD covered all boundaries. Parser/LSP assertions first failed to compile because fix/descriptor types and fields did not exist. After the in-memory path was GREEN, a new stdio black-box test failed because `Diagnostic.data.descriptorId` was absent, then passed after JSON serialization and fixes-array cleanup were added. WSL GCC 11.4, WSL Clang 14, and Windows MSVC 19.44.35228 each passed semantic query 14/14, compiler semantic-query diagnostics 16/16, LSP semantic-query diagnostics 11/11, ownership diagnostics 1/1, union diagnostics 12/12, diagnostic-fix stdio smoke, and minimal-open stdio smoke. MSVC CTest also discovered and passed `language_server_stdio_diagnostic_fix_smoke` 1/1. Full repository GREEN is not claimed; diagnostic registry IDs, broader machine-applicable fixes, type-mismatch details, ownership related chains, and localization remain later plan items.

## Stage 3 Scoped Semantic Analysis Foundation And Completion Fallback

2026-07-19 update: `ZrLanguageServer_SemanticAnalyzer_AnalyzeScope` now accepts a module AST plus a structurally validated declaration root. Symbol collection remains module-wide so names outside the selected callable stay resolvable, while reference collection, type checking, CFG construction, dataflow, and query diagnostics are limited to that root. The cache identity combines the full-AST hash, scoped-root hash, and scoped range. `FindAnalysisRootAtPosition` recognizes functions, methods, meta functions, tests, lambdas, and property accessors through class/struct/property and compile-time wrappers; its public export also keeps direct query tests valid across the Windows parser/LSP DLL boundary. Full analysis delegates to the same orchestration with the module root.

The completion semantic-fact path now invokes scoped analysis only when its existing query produces no items. It selects the declaration at the cursor and falls back to full-module analysis when no safe root exists. Property and compile-time wrappers return a root only when they actually contain an accessor or callable, so a non-callable wrapper cannot suppress that full-module fallback. This is an L6 robustness foundation, not L6 completion: document updates and most hover/query paths still run full analysis, symbol collection is still module-wide, and declaration-level parse, cache invalidation, cancellation, snapshot races, provider parity, and latency/memory budgets remain open. The main analyzer remains 2809 lines, but new orchestration and root resolution are isolated in 158-line and 171-line modules; focused test cases are isolated in a 254-line include module.

TDD first failed at link time because the scoped API and root resolver did not exist, then reached runtime RED with `AnalyzeScope=0`; structural AST membership replaced an invalid source-range containment assumption. Review added a second RED where an empty property wrapper was incorrectly returned as an analysis root; restricting wrapper traversal to actual nested accessors/callables made the local-query suite 21/21 on all three toolchains. The concurrent canonical TypeId work required exact-type assertions to query per-expression facts instead of removed AST ownership in canonical type records. The cleanup-block CFG contract also exposed forward/backward dataflow RED at `Expected 1 Was 0`; both directions now transfer statement and cleanup blocks through one predicate. A parser-internal union lookup was replaced by the exported semantic-query API after MSVC exposed the private cross-DLL reference. Final frozen-snapshot matrices on WSL GCC 11.4, WSL Clang 14, and Windows MSVC 19.44.35228 each ran fourteen targets with zero exit or failure-marker failures: semantic query 16, compiler query diagnostics 16, parser 75, expression facts 28, type inference 118, dataflow 9, local query 21, plus semantic analyzer, ownership, union, statement, language-feature, LSP-query, and interface suites. ## Stage 3 Identical-Content Snapshot And Semantic Cache Reuse

2026-07-19 update: `ZrLanguageServer_IncrementalParser_UpdateFile` now compares an existing document's current byte length and content before allocating a replacement text block. An identical-content update advances only a newer document version, preserving the content generation, dirty state, AST, semantic analyzer, and semantic context. The public LSP update path still invokes parse and semantic analysis, so reuse is exercised through the normal lifecycle: parse observes the unchanged snapshot and semantic analysis hits the existing full-module cache. A changed-content control proves that the original allocation, generation increment, AST rebuild, and semantic execution path remains active.

`SZrSemanticAnalysisMetrics` exposes valid analysis request, actual successful execution, and cache-hit counts plus the last execution range. The interface test uses those counters together with snapshot identities: identical content must add one request and one hit with no execution, while changed content must add one request and one execution with no hit. The new cases live in the 212-line `test_lsp_snapshot_cache_cases.h` include module instead of extending the already 7,000-line interface test body. This slice does not claim declaration-level parsing or invalidation; any real content edit still rebuilds the file AST and invalidates the semantic cache.

TDD first failed to compile because the metrics type/API did not exist, then runtime RED showed a v1-to-v2 identical update replacing the text block, increasing generation from 1 to 2, replacing the AST, executing semantic analysis twice, and recording no cache hit. The minimal no-op content path made the interface suite 79/79 on WSL GCC 11.4, WSL Clang 14, and Windows MSVC 19.44.35228. MSVC also rejected a test-only reference to private `UpdateDocumentCore` with `LNK2019`; the final test uses the exported public update API without widening production visibility. Each toolchain then passed the same fourteen-target semantic matrix with no exit or failure-marker failures and passed the registered stdio/CLI JSON-RPC smoke 1/1. Existing GCC/Clang CLI const warnings and MSVC D9025/debug warnings are outside the changed files. ## Stage 3 Minimal Change Range And Declaration Classification

2026-07-19 update: a real content update now measures its exact old and new byte ranges from the longest common prefix and the longest non-overlapping common suffix. `SZrFileChangeInfo` stores both ranges plus a conservative impact class. The LSP update path classifies the change while the old AST is still valid, then persists only the owning declaration type and range before parsing replaces the AST. Function, method, meta-function, test, lambda, and property-accessor body edits become `DECLARATION_BODY`; declaration edits outside the body become `DECLARATION_SIGNATURE`; unresolved or top-level edits remain `MODULE`.

Zero-length insertions at a declaration boundary stay module-level, and insertions at a body boundary stay signature-level. These rules deliberately prefer excess invalidation over an unsafe local classification. Reclassification clears previous declaration metadata before resolving a new owner, so a module fallback cannot retain a stale type or source range. An AST marked `usesFallbackAst` belongs to an earlier last-good text snapshot and is therefore never used to classify the immediate old-text range. `lastChangeRange` remains the compatibility view of the new-content range, while `lastChangeInfo` carries the complete old/new and ownership facts. This slice measures and classifies work only: real edits still rebuild the whole file AST and run the existing semantic path.

TDD first failed compilation because the change-info structure, impact enum, and classifier API did not exist. Runtime coverage then fixed the precise body range, exposed that `int -> float` has the smaller byte diff `in -> floa` due to the shared trailing `t`, and proved a top-level declaration insertion remains module-level. Review added RED cases for stale declaration metadata and for a recovery edit incorrectly classified through a fallback AST; explicit reset and snapshot matching made the interface suite 83/83 on WSL GCC 11.4, WSL Clang 14, and Windows MSVC 19.44.35228. The final code on each toolchain passed the same fourteen-target matrix with `run=14 failures=0`, no failure markers, and the stdio/CLI JSON-RPC smoke 1/1. L6 remains open for partial reparse, owning-function CFG/query cache invalidation, direct-caller and ModuleIdentity propagation, cancellation, immutable snapshot races, provider parity, and latency/memory budgets.

## Stage 3 Token-Equivalent Semantic Snapshot Reuse

2026-07-19 update: a real same-length content change can now preserve the current AST and semantic cache when the existing parser lexer proves that both token streams are semantically and positionally identical. The comparison rejects fallback ASTs and lexer errors, then checks token kind, literal/identifier value, token-start byte/line/line-start coordinates, current lexer byte/line state, and the final EOS position. Comment text can therefore change without semantic recomputation only when no token or EOF coordinate moves. The implementation is isolated in `incremental_token_equivalence.c/.h`; it uses two normal parser states so lexer buffers follow existing allocation and cleanup rules.

Unlike byte-identical version reuse, this path allocates a new text block and advances content generation because clients and source projections must observe the new comment/trivia text. It marks parsing clean, preserves parser diagnostics, updates the content hash, and lets the normal LSP semantic request hit the existing AST/cache key. Same-length token-value changes and whitespace-to-newline changes are both rejected: the first changes semantic token data, while the second changes line coordinates. Length changes, lex errors, and fallback snapshots also take the existing full parse/analysis path.

TDD first failed compilation because `SZrFileChangeInfo.isTokenEquivalent` did not exist. GREEN proved `// old note -> // new note` replaces the text block and increments generation while preserving AST, semantic context, and execution count and adding one request/cache hit. A same-length space-to-newline case proves coordinate-sensitive invalidation; a same-length `return 1 -> return 2` case was discovery/GREEN for token-value invalidation. After refreshing the isolated sources to current `HEAD=1413501`, WSL GCC 11.4, WSL Clang 14, and Windows MSVC 19.44.35228 each pass interface 86/86, incremental parser 6/6, the same fourteen-target matrix with `run=14 failures=0`, and stdio/CLI JSON-RPC smoke 1/1. This is not declaration-level recomputation: ordinary body token edits still rebuild and reanalyze the full file, and the two-lexer precheck has not yet been replaced by a cached token inventory or accepted against latency/memory budgets.

## Stage 3 Strict Document Version Rejection

2026-07-19 update: `ZrLanguageServer_IncrementalParser_UpdateFile` now requires every update to an existing document to carry a version strictly greater than the current version. Equal and stale versions return `ZR_FALSE` before byte-identical comparison, range calculation, token-equivalence lexing, text-block allocation, parsing, or semantic analysis. A document that does not yet exist can still be created at version 0, preserving the workspace/on-disk initialization boundary.

The incremental-parser test fixes a version-5 text block, content generation, AST, and clean state, then proves that an equal-version identical update and a stale changed update are both rejected without mutation. ## Stage 3 Scoped Query Semantic Cache

2026-07-19 update: completion fallback analysis now uses a scoped-query analyzer owned by the document's main analyzer instead of allocating and freeing a temporary analyzer for every empty-provider request. The child analyzer owns its own symbol/reference/compiler/semantic context and one-entry AST/root/range cache, so scoped work cannot replace the main analyzer's full-document context. Repeating the same scope records two requests, one execution, and one cache hit; the completion integration test fixes the existing empty-primary-provider fallback and observes the same `2/1/1` metrics through the public LSP request path.

Lifecycle invalidation preserves the preceding incremental contracts. Byte-identical and token-equivalent updates retain the child because the AST and semantics remain current. A real edit checks `fileVersion->isDirty` and frees the child before incremental parsing can release the old AST; direct analyzer calls that switch AST identities provide a second invalidation guard. Cache disable, clear, and analyzer free propagate to the owned child. Ownership logic is isolated in the 37-line `semantic_analyzer_scope_cache.c`; the large analyzer, query, and interface files retain only initialization and orchestration changes.

## Stage 3 Local Signature And Generic Direct-Dependency Invalidation

2026-07-20 update: same-length signature and generic edits to top-level ordinary functions now consult the scoped semantic context before discarding its one-entry query cache. A resolved reference fact whose declaration range equals the changed function name range is a direct dependency; this covers ordinary calls and resolved function-value reads without comparing names or display strings. A scope with no such edge may proceed to the existing post-parse full-range and AST-hash gate. An unannotated function body uses the same dependency decision because its inferred return contract may change, while an explicit return annotation keeps body-only caller caches eligible for reuse.

Dependency availability is tri-state. Invalid fact arrays, analyzer or query diagnostics, unresolved calls, and closure identifiers without a same-range resolved reference produce `unknown`, never `none`. Unsupported member or receiver declarations also remain unknown: receiver effects are canonical member contracts, but the resolved receiver-call target has not yet been published to the reference/query surface. LSP therefore invalidates conservatively instead of inferring a target from a member name.

`SZrSemanticAnalysisMetrics` retains total scoped invalidations and now separates resolved direct-dependency invalidations from conservative fallback invalidations. Declaration overlap and coordinate/hash failures remain local invalidations and only affect the total. Focused tests fix generic unrelated preservation, generic and inferred-return direct callers, explicit-return body caller preservation, resolved function-value edges, poisoned facts, receiver-signature fallback, and inferred method-body fallback. The stage still owns only one scoped analyzer, and the main document continues whole-file parsing and semantic analysis.

Final evidence on stable `HEAD=62eefc2` plus this stage: GCC 11.4, Clang 14, and clean-rebuilt MSVC 19.44.35228 each run the same sixteen-target matrix with 16/16 process exits at zero and the focused local semantic query at 31/31. Each retains the same unrelated one-marker semantic-analyzer and four-marker binary/plugin project baseline. All three rebuild and pass the real stdio/CLI smoke; MSVC uses `VSCMD_VER=17.14.36`. No latency percentile, peak-memory, multi-scope cache, or precise receiver-target claim is made by this slice.

## Stage 3 Canonical Source Public-Contract Hash

2026-07-20 update: `ZrParser_SemanticQuery_PublicContract` now publishes a deterministic source-module contract hash and export count from canonical semantic/type facts. Schema v1 structurally encodes callable parameter names and type contracts, passing/escape/initialization/temporary/call-site policy, return type, receiver effect, effect flags, generic flags, and supported canonical type graphs. Generic parameter owner IDs and declaration order are normalized; process-local IDs, pointers, and source token spelling are not identities.

The available source surface currently includes all ordinary top-level functions and explicitly public mutable variables. Ordinary function visibility is not retained as a canonical fact, so private functions are conservatively included. Named generic constraints, public types/layout, extern/compile-time/intermediate declarations, public const, decorated/default/variadic callables, diagnostics, error types, corrupt facts, or semantic owner mismatch make the query unavailable and clear its output. This prevents syntax-name matching or a partial hash from preserving stale importers.

Project source records store hash/count/availability. Refresh preserves reverse dependencies only when old and new module identity, hash, and count all match; change or unavailable propagates through the existing importer graph. Module identity drift seeds traversal with the old name. Match/change/unavailable and actual preservation/reanalysis remain separately countable. No receiver target is inferred from member names.

## Stage 2 Weak Receiver Possible-Release Ownership Flow

## Stage 2 Branch-Joined Borrow/Loan/Weak Owner-Set Lattice

## Stage 2 Unique Move And Use-After-Move Ownership Flow

2026-07-18 update: `ZrParser_SemanticFacts_ResolveControlFlowOwnership` adds the first CFG-backed ownership transition layer promised by `01-semantic-inference-core.md` section 4. Direct AST identity is accepted as statement membership for call arguments because the parser's enclosing call range does not always cover argument tokens. ## Stage 1 Reaching-Definition Payload

`SZrSemanticReferenceFact` carries two reaching-definition payload shapes. `definitionRange` / `hasDefinitionRange` remains the single-definition fast path used by `DefinitionOf` and older consumers. `definitionRanges` is a context-owned `SZrArray` of `SZrFileRange` values used when CFG-backed reaching definitions can enumerate multiple declaration/write locations reaching the same read. `ZrParser_SemanticFacts_Reset` / `Free` release this nested array for each reference fact before clearing the top-level fact array.

`ZrParser_SemanticFacts_ResolveLinearReachingDefinitions` continues to annotate straight-line reads with the latest preceding declaration/write. `ZrParser_SemanticFacts_ResolveControlFlowReachingDefinitions` now also preserves bounded multi-definition alternatives at ambiguous joins, including divergent branch writes and cloned `finally` paths. `ZrParser_SemanticQuery_DefinitionOf` still returns one best location, while `ZrParser_SemanticQuery_DefinitionsOf` returns all known matching declaration/write facts for multi-location consumers such as LSP go-to-definition.

## Stage 1 Definite Assignment Payload

`SZrSemanticReferenceFact` now also carries an optional definite-assignment state for reference facts. The payload is `hasDefiniteAssignmentState` plus `definiteAssignmentState`, with values `UNKNOWN`, `UNINIT`, `INIT`, and `MAYBE_INIT`. `semantic_query` consumes read states for diagnostics: `UNINIT` maps to `uninitialized_read`, while `MAYBE_INIT` maps to `possibly_uninitialized_read`.

`ZrParser_SemanticFacts_ResolveLinearDefiniteAssignments` is the first fact producer for this payload. It walks existing reference facts in order, treats explicitly marked declaration facts as the initial symbol state, treats write facts as `INIT`, and annotates reads with the latest known state for the same resolved symbol. Identifier write reference facts produced by type inference also pre-fill `INIT` so downstream consumers can observe the write state before a resolver pass. Unknown declarations leave reads as `UNKNOWN` / no-state so diagnostics do not invent errors.

`ZrParser_SemanticFacts_ResolveControlFlowDefiniteAssignments` is the first CFG-backed producer. It builds a symbol map from resolved declaration/read/write facts, initializes unassigned declarations as `UNINIT`, runs forward dataflow over script, function, test, and nested function-like CFG roots, and writes the joined state back to source read facts. Compiler assignment lowering now records identifier write facts for assignment targets instead of treating the left-hand side as a read, so a branch such as `if (flag) { seed = 1; } return seed;` produces a `MAYBE_INIT` read and a `possibly_uninitialized_read` semantic query diagnostic. Constant-true `while`/traditional `for` loops and omitted-condition `for(;;)` loops do not add a fake zero-iteration path in CFG, so a write followed by `break` can leave the subsequent read as `INIT` and suppress the false uninitialized-read diagnostic.

Numeric branch refinement now lives in `type_inference_branch_refinement.c` with focused parser/LSP branch tests. The branch scope supports simple identifier-vs-integer-literal comparisons on true and false branches, true-branch `&&` intersection, false-branch `||` complement intersection, true-branch equality, edge-only single-interval complements for representable `!=` true branches and `==` false branches, false-branch `!=` inversion to exact equality, representable same-direction subsets of true-branch `||` unions and false-branch `&&` complement unions, unary logical-not branch polarity inversion over those supported forms, `else if` scope stacking, and a fixed two-segment payload for tested same-identifier `||`/`&&` combinations. `SZrInferredType` and `SZrSemanticNumericFact` keep the existing min/max envelope while optionally carrying `rangeSegmentCount` / `rangeSegments`, so older consumers still see a conservative interval and semantic query consumers can inspect the precise split. `ZrParser_SemanticFacts_FindNumericByNode` prefers richer same-node numeric facts, so LSP symbol surfaces do not stop at an earlier broad initializer fact when a later branch-aware segmented fact exists for the same AST node. For example, `if (!(seed < 10)) { seed + 1; }` with `seed: 0..255` delegates to the false branch of `seed < 10`, so the parser-owned numeric fact and LSP local semantic query both report `11..256` for `seed + 1`. `if (seed < 10 || seed < 20) { seed + 1; }` narrows then-scope `seed` to `0..19` and reports `1..20`; `if (seed < 10 && seed < 20) { ... } else { seed + 1; }` narrows else-scope `seed` to `10..255` and reports `11..256`. `if (seed < 10 || seed > 20) { seed + 1; }` keeps then-scope `seed` as envelope `0..255` plus segments `0..9` / `21..255`, and the scalar addition path reports `seed + 1` as envelope `1..256` plus segments `1..10` / `22..256`; the false branch of `if (seed > 10 && seed < 20) { ... } else { seed + 1; }` similarly reports envelope `1..256` plus segments `1..11` / `21..256`. Nested same-identifier combinations can now first refine child conditions before merging: `if ((seed > 2 && seed < 10) || seed == 20) { seed + 1; }` reports envelope `4..21` plus segments `4..10` / `21..21`, and `else if (seed < 20) { seed + 1; }` after an outer `if (seed < 10)` false branch reports `11..20`. LSP local query, plain hover, public hover, rich hover, inlay hint labels, completion detail, and signature parameter documentation consume the same parser-owned segmented numeric fact for the fixed two-segment case. Interior true-branch inequality hole sets, arbitrary segment counts beyond the fixed payload, full hole-set modeling, arbitrary boolean formulas beyond the tested same-identifier subset, complete De Morgan expansion, CFG pruning, and general CFG-wide numeric dataflow remain out of scope for this branch-refinement layer.

The segment payload is no longer limited to the two inline `rangeSegments` slots. `SZrInferredType` and `SZrSemanticNumericFact` keep the first two `SZrNumericRangeSegment` values inline and store additional segments in `rangeExtraSegments`; `type_system_numeric_segments.c` owns the shared reset/free/copy/append/access helpers so semantic facts, branch scopes, numeric `+`/`-` segment shifting, and LSP formatters do not duplicate storage rules. Current tested coverage proves true-branch interior `!=` hole splitting (`seed != 10` over `0..20` becomes `1..10` and `12..21` after `+ 1`) and same-identifier true-branch `||` three-segment output (`seed < 5 || seed == 10 || seed > 20` becomes `1..5`, `11..11`, and `22..256` after `+ 1`). A six-segment equality-disjunction fixture now verifies the internal fact keeps all segments after scalar `+ 1`, while `lsp_numeric_range_text.c` applies the editor-display cap from `ZR_LSP_NUMERIC_RANGE_SEGMENT_DISPLAY_LIMIT`: LSP hover/rich hover, inlay, completion, and signature docs render the first four segments and append `... +N more` for the hidden tail. `lsp_local_semantic_hover_text.c` now owns fact-to-hover text assembly so `lsp_local_semantic_query.c` stays focused on selection and materialization. This is a bounded representation and tested subset, not a claim of arbitrary symbolic boolean formulas, cross-block numeric dataflow, or unbounded segment growth.

`type_inference_branch_assignment_join.c` is the first narrow cross-block numeric assignment join. It is deliberately smaller than the planned CFG-wide numeric dataflow engine: parser `ZR_AST_IF_EXPRESSION` inference and LSP typecheck call it only for simple numeric assignment expressions in simple branch blocks. The original form supports an `if/else` whose then and else blocks each assign the same identifier and joins both right-hand-side ranges into one min/max envelope, so `if (flag) { narrowed = 1; } else { narrowed = 10; } narrowed + 1` produces `2..11` in parser facts and LSP local semantic query. The helper also supports one-sided assignment joins for the tested simple shapes: no-`else` true-branch assignment joins the true RHS range with the retained false-path pre-branch binding, while explicit else-only assignment joins the else RHS range with the retained true-path pre-branch binding. The tested multi-statement expansion is intentionally narrow: branch blocks may contain ordinary expression statements before or after simple assignment candidates, so both `if (flag) { flag; narrowed = 1; } else { flag; narrowed = 10; } narrowed + 1` and `if (flag) { narrowed = 1; flag; } else { narrowed = 10; flag; } narrowed + 1` produce `2..11`. The helper replays same-target sequential simple assignments in a branch-scoped temporary type environment, so RHS expressions can depend on earlier writes in the same branch without publishing those replay bindings as declaration facts; `if (flag) { narrowed = 1; narrowed = narrowed + 1; } else { narrowed = 10; narrowed = narrowed + 1; } narrowed + 1` produces `3..12`. The next bounded expansion records all simple assignment targets seen in both branch blocks, replays each branch in order, and joins each target's final reachable range back into the current environment. That lets cross-target RHS dependencies flow inside one branch block: `if (flag) { low = 1; high = low + 1; } else { low = 10; high = low + 10; } high + low` produces `3..30`. Unsupported assignment expressions still make the helper decline this shortcut instead of pretending to solve general branch dataflow. To make annotated locals participate in retained paths, `ZrParser_TypeInference_TryApplyInitializerNumericRange` preserves a compatible numeric initializer's single-point range on an explicitly annotated binding in both parser lambda-return analysis and LSP typecheck binding registration. For example, `var narrowed: int = 5; if (flag) { narrowed = 10; } return narrowed + 1;` and `var narrowed: int = 5; if (flag) { flag; } else { narrowed = 10; } return narrowed + 1;` both produce `6..11`. The current bounded nested expansion lets branch replay call the same helper for nested simple `if/else` blocks before the outer branch result is joined, so `if (flag) { if (inner) { narrowed = 1; } else { narrowed = 2; } } else { if (inner) { narrowed = 10; } else { narrowed = 20; } } narrowed + 1` produces `2..21`. This still does not model loops, arbitrary nested control-flow beyond simple nested if/else assignment blocks, unsupported assignment expressions, symbolic fixed points, or general reaching numeric definitions.

Assignment-init true/omitted fixtures and direct var-init true/omitted fixtures now report `11..11` through parser facts and LSP local semantic query. This only claims no-step supported init/header-local break-prefix replay before a plain `break;`; step handling, combined var-init+step, destructuring/no-range header bindings, false-condition init side effects, non-plain break/continue, nested or symbolic control flow, true fixed points, unsupported assignment expressions, and general CFG-wide numeric dataflow remain future work.

2026-06-23 update: known-true/omitted traditional `for` with a step now has a bounded step-before-break path when there is no init. `ZrParser_TypeInferenceLoopAssignment_StatementIsPlainBreak` lives in the loop syntax helper module and is shared by the body-plan collector and the entry dispatcher. If a no-init `for` has a known-true or omitted condition, a step expression, and a top-level plain `break;` in the body, `type_inference_loop_assignment_entry.c` can prove that step is skipped on that first iteration exit path and routes the body prefix through `ZrParser_TypeInferenceLoopAssignment_JoinBodyAtLeastOnce`. Thus `for (; true; narrowed = 20) { narrowed = 10; break; } narrowed + 1;` and `for (;; narrowed = 20) { narrowed = 10; break; } narrowed + 1;` report `11..11` through parser facts and LSP local semantic query, not the pre-loop `6..6` or step result `21..21`. This only claims no-init, top-level plain-break-before-step, supported numeric body assignment; init+step/header-local+step, nested break, continue, break with expression, known-true loops without a break, fixed points, unsupported assignment expressions, and general CFG-wide numeric dataflow remain future work.

2026-06-23 update: known-true/omitted traditional `for` init+step and header-local+step forms now reuse the same step-before-break proof. `type_inference_loop_assignment_entry.c` applies supported assignment init or direct identifier `var` init in the existing temporary for-init scope, and then calls the at-least-once body replay even when a step exists if a top-level plain `break;` proves the step is skipped on the first-iteration exit path. Thus assignment-init+step true/omitted fixtures and direct var-init+step true/omitted fixtures report `11..11` through parser facts and LSP local semantic query. This only claims supported init/header-local bindings plus step when a top-level plain `break;` exits before the step; nested break, continue, break with expression, known-true loops without a break, complex body control flow, fixed points, unsupported assignment expressions, and general CFG-wide numeric dataflow remain future work.

2026-06-23 update: the same step-before-break path now recognizes one bounded nested-if control-flow shape. `ZrParser_TypeInferenceLoopAssignment_StatementGuaranteesPlainBreak` in `type_inference_loop_assignment_syntax.c` proves that a top-level `if/else` statement skips the step when both then and else branches guarantee a plain `break;`. `type_inference_loop_assignment_entry.c` accepts that guarantee for known-true/omitted traditional `for` loops with a step, and the body plan collector records the nested-if assignment before stopping replay. Thus `for (; true; narrowed = 20) { if (flag) { narrowed = 10; break; } else { narrowed = 12; break; } } narrowed + 1;` reports `11..13` through parser facts and LSP local semantic query. This only claims top-level if/else with both branches ending in plain break and supported nested-if assignment replay; missing else, branch-without-break, continue, break with expression, known-true loops without a break, complex nested control flow, fixed points, unsupported assignment expressions, and general CFG-wide numeric dataflow remain future work.

2026-06-23 update: the step-before-break path now also recognizes a deterministic true single-branch `if`. `type_inference_loop_assignment_entry.c` reuses the same literal/logical-fact/constant bool evaluator as loop condition handling to prove that a top-level `if (true)` enters only the then branch; `type_inference_loop_assignment_nested_if.c` treats a missing `else` as a no-assignment target path during target collection; and `type_inference_branch_assignment_join.c` commits only the reachable branch when an `if` condition is known. Thus `for (; true; narrowed = 20) { if (true) { narrowed = 10; break; } } narrowed + 1;` reports `11..11` through parser facts and LSP local semantic query, rather than retaining the pre-loop `6..6` path or the skipped step's `21..21` path. This only claims top-level deterministic-true `if` then-branch assignment plus plain break before the step; symbolic or unknown if conditions, unknown missing-else branches, branches without break, continue, break with expression, no-break known-true loops, complex nested control flow, fixed points, unsupported assignments, and general CFG-wide numeric dataflow remain future work.

Exact logical facts can now feed branch reachability diagnostics. `type_inference_logical_fact_known_bool_value` reads parser-owned `ALWAYS_TRUE` / `ALWAYS_FALSE` facts after interval comparison inference, so compiler conditional expressions like `seed < 300 ? 1 : 2` record constant-branch reachability and publish `unreachable_code` through semantic query diagnostics. LSP `if` analysis materializes condition facts before branch traversal and records the same constant branch reachability for `if (seed < 300) ... else ...`; LSP diagnostic de-duplication compares range and code so the direct `unreachable_branch` warning does not hide semantic query `unreachable_code`. This still only consumes exact logical facts; symbolic interval splitting, broader overflow analysis, and general CFG pruning remain future work.

Numeric overflow facts also feed semantic query diagnostics. `ZrParser_SemanticQuery_Diagnostics` maps any scoped numeric fact with `mayOverflow=true` to warning `numeric_overflow`, so existing type-inference facts for expressions like `9223372036854775807 + 1` are visible in parser query results, compiler `queryDiagnostics`, and LSP diagnostics. This is a diagnostic bridge over existing facts only; it does not add new overflow inference, symbolic arithmetic, or CFG-wide numeric dataflow.

Fixed-size and finite-max array bounds facts now feed semantic query diagnostics as well. Computed member inference for arrays first checks indexes that `type_inference_node_integer_value` can evaluate; negative indexes or constants at/above a known upper bound record a computed-member expression fact carrying a bounds diagnostic message. For non-constant index expressions, the same path infers the index expression type and uses its integer range: a whole range proven out of bounds maps to error `array_index_out_of_bounds`, such as `index: u8` in `values[index + 2]` for a two-element array, while a range that overlaps legal indexes but also contains invalid values maps to warning `array_index_may_be_out_of_bounds`, such as `values[index]` with `index: u8` and array size 2. Known non-integer index types now map to error `array_index_type_mismatch`; unknown/no-inferable index expressions and untyped object indexes remain silent to avoid false positives. Fixed-size array literals, `min==max` constraints, and finite `arrayMaxSize` constraints all provide an upper bound; primitive integer parameters such as `index: int` already receive their full type range during AST type conversion, so they also flow through the possible-warning path. Min-only / no finite-upper-bound arrays do not diagnose positive indexes as out of bounds, but they now warn when a known integer index range may be negative; that message omits the finite-size label because no upper bound exists. `SZrSemanticExpressionFact` carries optional `diagnosticCode` and `diagnosticSeverity` payloads, so `ZrParser_SemanticQuery_Diagnostics` can preserve exact error versus possible warning versus type-mismatch semantics instead of hard-coding every computed-member diagnostic as `array_index_out_of_bounds`. The array bounds/type diagnostic builders live in `type_inference_array_diagnostics.c` to keep the broader semantic-fact emission file from absorbing more bounds-specific responsibility. This bounds work still does not diagnose truly unknown/no-inferable-range indexes, and it does not add runtime bounds checks or CFG-wide numeric dataflow.
